source: formula 1 game with damage in cars and tracks from the actual f1

image_prompt.text: A wide standardised starting grid of evenly spaced slots so the field launches side by side
Armco barriers and walls lining the circuit that physically stop a car leaving the track
Tight hairpin sections forcing a clean direction reversal on the lap
the circuit reproduces the layout of a real Formula 1 track

layout_placement.text: Grid slots assigned per car, aligned so nobody collides at the launch
Sector and lap detection at each split point and at the start-finish line

notes: P6 is the genre route: the circuit has to read as one continuous followable loop in plan view before it is dressed.
A real Formula 1 circuit is several kilometres long and will not fit one framed top-down at a readable scale - it should be decomposed into sectors rather than squeezed into one image.
Car damage is a vehicle behaviour with no layout footprint and could not be carried.
No option can name a specific real-world track to copy.

open_questions.ask: Which circuit specifically - Monaco, Silverstone, Spa? Each has a very different footprint.
How many laps is a race, and how many cars on the grid?

coverage_missing.ask: Which real circuit should it be? Monaco and Silverstone have almost nothing in common as footprints.
How many laps, and how many cars on the grid?
Full-length circuit, or a shortened version that fits a single readable map?

answers.ask: Which circuit specifically - Monaco, Silverstone, Spa? Each has a very different footprint.
answers.answer: Use Monaco, as a compact, recognizable real F1 circuit that keeps the first build small and focused.

answers.ask: How many laps is a race, and how many cars on the grid?
answers.answer: Make races 3 laps with a 6-car grid, including the player, for a small playable arcade-style race.
